We combine classical methods of combinatorial group theory with the theory of small cancellations over relatively hyperbolic groups to construct finitely generated torsion-free groups that have only finitely many classes of conjugate elements. Moreover, we present several results concerning embeddings into such groups.   As another application of these techniques, we prove that every countable group $C$ can be realized as a group of outer automorphisms of a group $N$, where $N$ is a finitely generated group having Kazhdan's property (T) and containing exactly two conjugacy classes.

outputs.L1: We combine classical methods from combinatorial group theory with small-cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups to construct finitely generated torsion-free groups with only finitely many conjugacy classes. We also establish several results concerning embeddings into such groups. As a further application of these techniques, we prove that every countable group \(C\) can be realized as the outer automorphism group of a finitely generated group \(N\) with Kazhdan’s property (T) and exactly two conjugacy classes.
outputs.L2: By integrating traditional techniques from combinatorial group theory with small-cancellation theory for relatively hyperbolic groups, we produce finitely generated, torsion-free groups with only a finite number of conjugacy classes. We also establish several theorems on embeddings into groups of this kind. In a further application, we show that any countable group \(C\) is isomorphic to the outer automorphism group of some finitely generated group \(N\) that has Kazhdan’s property \((T)\) and precisely two conjugacy classes.
outputs.L3:
The work combines techniques from classical combinatorial group theory with small-cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups. This framework is used to construct finitely generated, torsion-free groups that have only finitely many conjugacy classes, despite potentially having highly nontrivial algebraic structures. It also yields several embedding theorems, showing that prescribed groups can be incorporated into groups with these unusual conjugacy properties.

A particularly strong application concerns outer automorphism groups. For every countable group \(C\), one can construct a finitely generated group \(G\) with Kazhdan’s property \((T)\) such that
\[
\operatorname{Out}(G)\cong C.
\]
Moreover, \(G\) can be chosen to have exactly two conjugacy classes: the identity forms one class, while all nonidentity elements belong to the other. Thus, the construction simultaneously provides strong rigidity through property \((T)\), extreme simplicity of the conjugacy structure, and complete flexibility in prescribing the outer automorphism group.
outputs.L4:
The authors investigate how much algebraic complexity can occur in groups with extremely few conjugacy classes. Their approach combines techniques from combinatorial group theory with small-cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups. This framework makes it possible to impose strong global restrictions on conjugacy while preserving selected subgroups and other prescribed structural features.

Using these methods, they construct finitely generated, torsion-free groups having only finitely many conjugacy classes. In such groups, every element belongs to one of a fixed finite collection of conjugacy classes, despite the group itself potentially being infinite and algebraically complicated. The construction also yields embedding theorems, showing that suitable countable groups can be incorporated into finitely generated groups with tightly controlled conjugacy behavior. These results illustrate the effectiveness of relative small-cancellation methods for building groups that simultaneously satisfy restrictive global properties and retain designated algebraic data.

A particularly striking application concerns outer automorphism groups. The authors prove that every countable group can be realized as the outer automorphism group of a finitely generated group with Kazhdan’s property (T) and exactly two conjugacy classes. Thus, even among finitely generated property-(T) groups whose nontrivial elements are all conjugate, the outer automorphism group can be arbitrary, subject only to countability.

Taken together, the results reveal a remarkable degree of flexibility within classes of groups that appear highly rigid. Having finitely many—or even only two—conjugacy classes does not prevent a group from encoding complicated subgroup structures or arbitrary countable symmetry groups. The work therefore provides both new existence and embedding results and a strong demonstration of the constructive power of small-cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups.
outputs.L5: David Kazhdan is a prominent mathematician known for his influential work in representation theory, algebra, and geometry. One of his best-known contributions is **Kazhdan’s property (T)**, a rigidity property of certain topological groups that has important applications in group theory, ergodic theory, and the study of expander graphs. Moreover, his collaboration with George Lusztig led to the development of **Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials**, which connect representation theory with the geometry of algebraic varieties. These ideas have had a lasting impact across several areas of modern mathematics.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an abstract for a research paper on finitely generated torsion-free groups with finitely many conjugacy classes, using small cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups.
counterfactuals.output: We construct infinite finitely generated torsion-free groups with a prescribed finite number of conjugacy classes. The construction proceeds through an inductive sequence of relatively hyperbolic groups and applies small cancellation theory over relatively hyperbolic groups to force selected elements to become conjugate while preserving the nontriviality of designated conjugacy classes. Suitable control of relative geodesics and periodic words ensures that the successive quotients remain torsion-free and that no unintended conjugacies are introduced. Passing to the direct limit yields, for every integer \(n\ge 2\), a finitely generated torsion-free group with exactly \(n\) conjugacy classes. In particular, the case \(n=2\) produces a group in which all nonidentity elements are conjugate. The method also provides flexibility for retaining prescribed subgroups and demonstrates the effectiveness of relative small cancellation techniques in constructing groups with highly constrained global conjugacy behavior.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main results of a group theory paper that constructs groups with only finitely many conjugacy classes and realizes arbitrary countable groups as outer automorphism groups.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper proves a striking realization theorem:

- **Every countable group \(C\)** is isomorphic to the outer automorphism group
  \[
  \operatorname{Out}(G)=\operatorname{Aut}(G)/\operatorname{Inn}(G)
  \]
  of a finitely generated—indeed, typically **2-generated**—group \(G\).

- The group \(G\) can simultaneously be chosen to have **exactly two conjugacy classes**: the identity class and one class containing every nonidentity element.

Thus, even among groups with an extremely rigid internal conjugacy structure, outer automorphism groups can be completely arbitrary countable groups. Such a \(G\) is necessarily infinite, centerless, and simple, since every nontrivial normal subgroup must contain the sole nonidentity conjugacy class.

The construction uses iterative small-cancellation/relative-hyperbolic techniques. At each stage, new relations force more elements to become conjugate, while carefully preserving a prescribed family of automorphisms and excluding unwanted ones. The result strengthens earlier realization theorems for outer automorphism groups by imposing the severe additional condition of having only finitely—indeed two—conjugacy classes.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise mathematical abstract describing applications of combinatorial group theory and relative small cancellation methods to embeddings, conjugacy classes, property (T), and outer automorphism groups.
counterfactuals.output: We develop relative small cancellation techniques in combinatorial group theory and apply them to several structural problems. Our methods produce controlled embeddings of countable groups into finitely generated groups while preserving prescribed algebraic and geometric properties, and allow precise manipulation of conjugacy classes. We construct groups with Kazhdan’s property (T) subject to additional embedding constraints, using small cancellation quotients that retain suitable rigidity. Finally, we realize broad classes of groups as outer automorphism groups of finitely generated groups. These results illustrate how relative presentations and diagrammatic arguments provide a unified framework for combining embedding flexibility with strong rigidity properties.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Can every countable group be realized as the outer automorphism group of a finitely generated Kazhdan group with exactly two conjugacy classes? State the relevant theorem and its broader construction context.
counterfactuals.output:
Yes.

**Realization theorem.** For every countable group \(Q\), there exists a finitely generated group \(N\) such that

\[
N \text{ has Kazhdan’s property }(T),\qquad
N \text{ has exactly two conjugacy classes},\qquad
\operatorname{Out}(N)\cong Q .
\]

Thus the conjugacy classes of \(N\) are \(\{1\}\) and \(N\setminus\{1\}\); in particular, \(N\) is an infinite simple group. Countability is the only possible restriction, since the automorphism group of a finitely generated group is countable.

The theorem belongs to the broader family of **Rips/small-cancellation realization constructions**. One constructs an extension

\[
1\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow 1
\]

with \(N\) a quotient of a suitable hyperbolic Kazhdan group. Small-cancellation methods are used simultaneously to force all nonidentity elements of \(N\) to be conjugate and to rigidify the extension so that every automorphism of \(N\) is induced by conjugation in \(G\). Consequently,

\[
\operatorname{Aut}(N)\cong G,\qquad
\operatorname{Inn}(N)\cong N,\qquad
\operatorname{Out}(N)\cong G/N\cong Q.
\]

This strengthens the general “prescribed outer automorphism group” results of Bumagin–Wise type by imposing both property \((T)\) and the extreme two-conjugacy-class condition.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a polished abstract for an article proving the existence of finitely generated torsion-free groups with finitely many conjugacy classes and related embedding results.
counterfactuals.output: We prove that, for every integer \(n\ge 2\), there exists an infinite finitely generated torsion-free group with exactly \(n\) conjugacy classes. We also establish a strong embedding theorem: every countable torsion-free group embeds in a finitely generated torsion-free group in which all nontrivial elements are conjugate. More generally, our constructions allow prescribed conjugacy relations while preserving torsion-freeness and injectivity of the original group. The proofs use carefully controlled extensions and small-cancellation techniques to collapse selected conjugacy classes without introducing torsion. These results demonstrate that finite generation and torsion-freeness impose remarkably little restriction on the global conjugacy structure of an infinite group.
